# typed: strict

module Staff
  class StudentsController < ApplicationController
    extend T::Sig

    include PaginationHelper

    QUERY_LIMIT = T.let(100, Integer)

    before_action :require_staff

    sig { void }
    def initialize
      super
      @student = T.let(nil, T.nilable(User))
      @current_enrollments = T.let(Enrollment.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @current_plans = T.let(Plan.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @activity_records = T.let([], T::Array[PlanActivity])
      @open_activity_records = T.let([], T::Array[PlanActivity])
      @upcoming_activities = T.let([], T::Array[PlanActivity])
      @submission_attempts = T.let(Submission.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @reviewable_submissions = T.let([], T::Array[Submission])
      @daily_reflections = T.let(DailyReflection.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @submissions_by_activity_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[T.nilable(Integer), T::Array[Submission]])
      @reflections_by_activity_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[T.nilable(Integer), T::Array[DailyReflection]])
      @evidence_by_activity_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[T.nilable(Integer), T::Array[EvidenceArtifact]])
      @work_products = T.let(EvidenceArtifact.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @class_scope = T.let(SchoolClass.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @students = T.let(User.none, PaginationHelper::PaginatedScope)
      @counts_by_student = T.let({}, T::Hash[Integer, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer]])
      @round = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Round))
      @current_enrollments_by_student_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[Integer, T::Array[Enrollment]])
      @primary_class_for_summary = T.let(nil, T.nilable(SchoolClass))
      @primary_class_enrollment_count = T.let(0, Integer)
      @primary_class_schedule_blocks = T.let(ScheduleBlock.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
      @waiting_total = T.let(0, Integer)
      @revision_total = T.let(0, Integer)
      @page = T.let(1, Integer)
      @per_page = T.let(PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, Integer)
      @pagination = T.let({
        records: User.none,
        page: 1,
        per_page: PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE,
        total_count: 0,
        total_pages: 1
      }, PaginationHelper::Page)
      @student_count = T.let(0, Integer)
      @rounds = T.let(nil, T.nilable(T::Array[Round]))
      @roster_builder = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Reviews::RosterBuilder))
      @roster_rows = T.let([], T::Array[Reviews::RosterBuilder::Row])
      @roster_waiting_totals = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
      @roster_plan_breakdown = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
      @roster_evidence_breakdown = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
      @roster_final_product_breakdown = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
      @participations_by_day = T.let({}, T::Hash[Date, String])
      @activities_by_day = T.let({}, T::Hash[Date, T::Array[PlanActivity]])
      @schedule_origin_path = T.let("", String)
      @schedule_origin_label = T.let("", String)
      @roster_filters = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, String])
    end

    sig { void }
    def show
      scope_hash = SiteScopeResolver.call(
        T.must(current_user),
        active_role: current_active_role,
        active_site: current_active_site
      )
      # WT-02 / S-2 — the stress-empty capture (script/visual_audit_manifest.json)
      # uses a stable username-keyed path so the seed's natural key survives
      # a replant. Accept either a numeric id or a username on this route so
      # the deterministic stress PNG can be produced from a stable identifier.
      raw_id = params[:id].to_s
      student =
        if raw_id.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
          scope_hash[:students].find_by(id: raw_id)
        else
          scope_hash[:students].find_by(username: raw_id)
        end
      @student = student
      return head(:not_found) unless student

      # The schedule is reachable only from Students or Signoff. Do not render
      # a caller-supplied URL into the Back control: an external `origin`
      # would create an open redirect from an authenticated staff surface.
      # A Students origin may retain the canonical roster filters so Back
      # restores the mentor's filtered context without accepting arbitrary
      # paths, duplicate parameters, nested values, or unknown keys.
      schedule_origin = validated_schedule_origin(params[:origin].to_s)
      if schedule_origin == signoff_queue_path
        @schedule_origin_path = signoff_queue_path
        @schedule_origin_label = "Signoff"
      elsif schedule_origin
        @schedule_origin_path = schedule_origin
        @schedule_origin_label = "Students"
      else
        @schedule_origin_path = students_path
        @schedule_origin_label = "Students"
      end

      site = current_active_site
      current_round_ids = Round.where(site_id: site&.id)
                               .current_on(site&.today || Date.current)
                               .select(:id)
      scoped_class_ids = scope_hash[:classes].select(:id)

      @current_enrollments = if site
                               Enrollment.active_on(site.today, site: site)
                                         .where(student: student, school_class_id: scoped_class_ids)
                                         .includes(school_class: :course)
                                         .order(:school_class_id)
      else
                               Enrollment.none
      end
      @current_plans = student.plans
                               .where(round_id: current_round_ids, school_class_id: scoped_class_ids)
                               .includes(:round, :school_class)
                               .order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc)
      activity_scope =
        if site
          PlanActivity
            .joins(plan: :school_class)
            .where(plans: { student_id: student.id, school_class_id: scoped_class_ids })
            .where(school_classes: { site_id: site.id })
        else
          PlanActivity.none
        end
      @activity_records = activity_scope
                          .includes(plan: %i[round school_class])
                          .order(position: :asc, id: :asc)
                          .to_a
      @open_activity_records = @activity_records.reject(&:done?)
      @upcoming_activities = []
      submission_scope = scope_hash[:submissions].where(student_id: student.id)
      @submission_attempts = submission_scope
                             .includes(:evidence_artifacts,
                                       activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                             .order(Arel.sql("COALESCE(submissions.submitted_at, submissions.created_at) DESC"), id: :desc)
      @reviewable_submissions = submission_scope
                                .latest_activity_outcomes
                                .includes(:evidence_artifacts,
                                          activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                                .to_a
                                .sort_by { |submission| [ submission.submitted_at || submission.created_at, submission.id ] }
                                .reverse
      # `state: :submitted` matches the canonical reviewer scope
      # (ReviewsController#show, ReviewWorklist#portfolio_activity_rows). A
      # DailyReflection defaults to :draft - the student's private,
      # un-submitted writing - and this surface rendered `reflection.body`
      # verbatim to staff, so drafts were being read by reviewers.
      @daily_reflections = scope_hash[:daily_reflections]
                           .where(student_id: student.id, state: :submitted)
                           .includes(plan_activity: { plan: %i[round school_class] })
                           .ordered

      @submissions_by_activity_id = @submission_attempts.to_a.group_by(&:activity_id)
      @reflections_by_activity_id = @daily_reflections.to_a.group_by(&:plan_activity_id)

      visible_artifacts = EvidenceArtifact
                          .kept
                          .where(screening_status: :clean)
                          .where(submission_id: submission_scope.select(:id))
      @evidence_by_activity_id = visible_artifacts
                                 .includes(:submission)
                                 .ordered
                                 .to_a
                                 .group_by(&:activity_id)
      @work_products = visible_artifacts
                       .work_products
                       .includes(activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } },
                                 submission: { activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } } })
                       .ordered

      # DA-005 / S-7 — schedule data for the bounded Student
      # schedule surface: participation by day, activities by
      # day, and the current round.
      @round = Round.where(site_id: site&.id)
                    .current_on(site&.today || Date.current)
                    .order(ends_on: :desc, starts_on: :asc)
                    .first || Round.where(site_id: site&.id).order(starts_on: :asc).first
      participation_scope = if @round && site
                              StudentParticipationDay
                                .where(student_id: student.id, round_id: @round.id, site_id: site.id)
                                .order(:participated_on)
      else
                                StudentParticipationDay.none
      end
      participations = participation_scope.to_a
      @participations_by_day = participations.each_with_object({}) do |p, h|
        h[p.participated_on] = p.day_part
      end

      @activities_by_day =
        if @round
          @activity_records.each_with_object({}) do |activity, h|
            next unless activity.plan&.round_id == @round.id
            start_date = @round.starts_on
            next unless start_date

            # The plan calendar is authoritative whenever an activity
            # has a canonical scheduled day. Older unscheduled rows
            # retain the deterministic position fallback so their
            # schedule remains readable until the programme dean
            # supplies dates.
            date = activity.scheduled_on || (start_date + ((activity.position - 1) / 3))
            h[date] ||= []
            h[date] << activity
          end
        else
          {}
        end
    end

    sig { void }
    def index
      scope_hash = SiteScopeResolver.call(
        T.must(current_user),
        active_role: current_active_role,
        active_site: current_active_site
      )
      # AC (analysis feedback, security regression fix): the prior
      # code re-derived the student list by expanding through
      # `Enrollment.where(school_class_id: class_ids)` — which
      # pulled in EVERY student enrolled in any of the viewer's
      # visible classes. For a contractor this was a real leak:
      # the resolver's `:students` key is the assignment set
      # (ContractorSupport rows at the active site), but
      # `:classes` is the set of classes the contractor's
      # assigned students are enrolled in. Expanding via
      # Enrollment.from(:classes) returned every classmate of
      # every assigned student, not just the contractor's
      # assigned set. The fix uses `scope_hash[:students]`
      # directly, which is the canonical narrowed set for the
      # active (role, site) tuple: self for :stu, assigned set
      # for :con, mentor's class roster for :men, site-wide for
      # :dex, org-wide for :sup. For non-contractor roles this
      # is semantically equivalent to the prior expansion (the
      # resolver computes the same set under the hood) so
      # nothing changes for dean / mentor / super-admin.
      @roster_filters = effective_roster_filters

      # and the class filter intersects the active set with the set of
      # users currently enrolled in the chosen class.

      end
      selected_class = nil
      if @roster_filters[:class_id].present?
        selected_class = @class_scope.find_by(id: @roster_filters[:class_id])
        base_students = if selected_class
                          base_students.where(
                            id: current_scope_enrollments

                        .where(student_id: student_ids)

                        .to_a

      @counts_by_student = student_ids.each_with_object({}) do |sid, acc|

          approved: counts[[ sid, :approved ]].to_i,
          draft: counts[[ sid, :draft ]].to_i,
          in_review: counts[[ sid, :in_review ]].to_i,
          submitted: counts[[ sid, :submitted ]].to_i,

      # per-student current-enrollment lookup so the view can render

      )

      @roster_waiting_totals = @roster_builder.waiting_totals
      @roster_plan_breakdown = @roster_builder.plan_breakdown
      @roster_evidence_breakdown = @roster_builder.evidence_breakdown
      @roster_final_product_breakdown = @roster_builder.final_product_breakdown

      # mentor roster does not render as an unbounded 200+ row table.
      # The metric counts (AM / PM / MT) stay above the filter so the
      # operator sees the full population regardless of the page window.
      # The roster renders the projection rows, not the older @students
      # relation. Paginating that relation left later roster rows visible and

      # so the visible rows, count, and links describe the same population.

      requested_per_page = PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE if requested_per_page < 1

      @pagination = {

      }

    end

    private

    sig { params(origin: String).returns(T.nilable(String)) }
    def validated_schedule_origin(origin)
      return signoff_queue_path if origin == signoff_queue_path
      return nil if origin.blank?

      uri = URI.parse(origin)
      return nil unless uri.relative? && uri.path == students_path && uri.fragment.nil?

      pairs = URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s)
      allowed_keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort page per_page].freeze
      return nil unless pairs.all? { |key, value| allowed_keys.include?(key) && value.is_a?(String) }
      return nil unless pairs.map(&:first).uniq.length == pairs.length

      origin
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    sig { returns(T::Hash[Symbol, String]) }
    def effective_roster_filters
      keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort].freeze
      if params[:clear_filters].present?
        session.delete(:students_roster_filters)
        return {}
      end

      supplied = params.permit(*keys).to_h.compact_blank
      stored = session[:students_roster_filters]
      stored_hash = stored.is_a?(Hash) ? stored.slice(*keys) : {}
      effective = supplied.present? ? supplied : stored_hash
      session[:students_roster_filters] = effective if supplied.present?
      effective.symbolize_keys
    end
  end

      @roster_builder = Reviews::RosterBuilder.new(
        user: current_user,
        site: site,
        role: (current_active_role || :men).to_sym,
        today: site&.today || Date.current,
        class_id: @roster_filters[:class_id].presence&.to_i || selected_class&.id,
        # The name search is a roster filter too. Apply it at the projection
        # boundary (not merely to the legacy @students relation) so every
        # rendered row, count, empty state, and pass origin describes the
        # same narrowed Students list.
        student_id: @roster_filters[:student_id].presence&.to_i,
        round_id: @roster_filters[:round_id].presence&.to_i,
        review_type: @roster_filters[:review_type].presence,
        status: @roster_filters[:status].presence,
        sort: @roster_filters[:sort].presence
      )
      @roster_rows = @roster_builder.rows
      @roster_waiting_totals = @roster_builder.waiting_totals
      @roster_plan_breakdown = @roster_builder.plan_breakdown
      @roster_evidence_breakdown = @roster_builder.evidence_breakdown
      @roster_final_product_breakdown = @roster_builder.final_product_breakdown

      # Rounds for the round-filter dropdown (round phase + date).
      @rounds = site ? Round.where(site_id: site.id).order(starts_on: :asc).to_a : []

      # WT-15 / AC-06 — paged scope + per-page selector so a 200+ student
      # mentor roster does not render as an unbounded 200+ row table.
      # The metric counts (AM / PM / MT) stay above the filter so the
      # operator sees the full population regardless of the page window.
      # The roster renders the projection rows, not the older @students
      # relation. Paginating that relation left later roster rows visible and
      # made the footer a status-only dead end. Page the canonical projection
      # so the visible rows, count, and links describe the same population.
      requested_per_page = params[:per_page].presence&.to_i || PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE
      requested_per_page = PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE if requested_per_page < 1
      @per_page = [ requested_per_page, PaginationHelper::MAX_PER_PAGE ].min
      total_count = @roster_rows.size
      total_pages = total_count.zero? ? 1 : (total_count.to_f / @per_page).ceil
      @page = [ [ params[:page].to_i, 1 ].max, total_pages ].min
      offset = (@page - 1) * @per_page
      @roster_rows = @roster_rows.slice(offset, @per_page) || []
      @pagination = {
        records: User.none,
        page: @page,
        per_page: @per_page,
        total_count: total_count,
        total_pages: total_pages
      }
      @student_count = total_count
    end

    private

    sig { params(origin: String).returns(T.nilable(String)) }
    def validated_schedule_origin(origin)
      return signoff_queue_path if origin == signoff_queue_path
      return nil if origin.blank?

      uri = URI.parse(origin)
      return nil unless uri.relative? && uri.path == students_path && uri.fragment.nil?

      pairs = URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s)
      allowed_keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort page per_page].freeze
      return nil unless pairs.all? { |key, value| allowed_keys.include?(key) && value.is_a?(String) }
      return nil unless pairs.map(&:first).uniq.length == pairs.length

      origin
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    sig { returns(T::Hash[Symbol, String]) }
    def effective_roster_filters
      keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort].freeze
      if params[:clear_filters].present?
        session.delete(:students_roster_filters)
        return {}
      end

      supplied = params.permit(*keys).to_h.compact_blank
      stored = session[:students_roster_filters]
      stored_hash = stored.is_a?(Hash) ? stored.slice(*keys) : {}
      effective = supplied.present? ? supplied : stored_hash
      session[:students_roster_filters] = effective if supplied.present?
      effective.symbolize_keys
    end
  end
end

      status: T.nilable(String),
      sort: T.nilable(String),
      query: T.nilable(String)
    ).void
  end
  def initialize(user:, site:, role:, today: nil, class_id: nil, student_id: nil, round_id: nil, review_type: nil, status: nil, sort: nil, query: nil)

class ContractorCourseAssignment < ApplicationRecord
  extend T::Sig

  belongs_to :contractor_user, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :site
  belongs_to :course

  validates :contractor_user_id, uniqueness: { scope: :course_id }
  validate :contractor_user_at_site
  validate :course_at_site
  validate :contractor_user_is_contractor

  private

  sig { void }
  def contractor_user_at_site
    contractor = contractor_user
    assignment_site = site
    return if contractor.nil? || assignment_site.nil?
    return if contractor.site_id == assignment_site.id
    return if contractor.user_roles.exists?(site_id: assignment_site.id)

    errors.add(:contractor_user, "must be at the same site as the assignment (or hold a UserRole at that site)")
    errors.add(:site, "must match contractor_user's site or one of their UserRole-anchored sites")
  end

  sig { void }
  def course_at_site
    assigned_course = course
    assignment_site = site
    return if assigned_course.nil? || assignment_site.nil? || assigned_course.site_id == assignment_site.id

    errors.add(:course, "must be at the same site as the assignment")
    errors.add(:site, "must match course's site")
  end

  sig { void }
  def contractor_user_is_contractor
    contractor = contractor_user
    assignment_site = site
    return if contractor.nil? || assignment_site.nil?
    return if contractor.user_roles.exists?(site: assignment_site, role: :con)
    return if contractor.con? && contractor.site_id == assignment_site.id

    errors.add(:contractor_user, "must hold the contractor role at the assignment site")
  end
end

# typed: strict

# Filters users by their active (role, site) tuple per spec 01 §6.
#
# The five scope types defined in the spec:
#   - Student (stu):     self-scope (sees only self)
#   - Contractor (con):  student-assignment-scope (sees only
#                        ContractorSupport-assigned students
#                        AT THE ACTIVE SITE — a contractor
#                        backing students on Oak does not
#                        leak Pine records via this resolver)
#   - Mentor (men):      class-based-scope (sees students in
#                        their classes AT THE ACTIVE SITE —
#                        a mentor assigned to Oak classes
#                        does not leak Pine students via
#                        classes the mentor taught at a
#                        different site historically)
#   - Dean (dex):        site-wide-scope within the active site
#   - Super-Admin (sup): org-wide-scope across all sites in the
#                        org of the active site
#
# The resolver is the canonical entry point for any controller /
# view that needs to filter by the actor's scope. It does NOT
# mutate state — every method is a class-level pure function.
class SiteScopeResolver
  extend T::Sig

  Role = T.type_alias { T.any(String, Symbol) }
  Scope = T.type_alias do
    {
      students: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      classes: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      submissions: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      daily_reflections: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      school_classes_as_mentor: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      site: T.nilable(Site)
    }
  end
  ActiveScope = T.type_alias { { role: T.nilable(Symbol), site: T.nilable(Site) } }
  RecordScopes = T.type_alias do
    {
      submissions: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      daily_reflections: ActiveRecord::Relation
    }
  end
  IdFilter = T.type_alias { T.any(Integer, T::Array[Integer], ActiveRecord::Relation) }

  ROLE_LABELS = T.let({
    stu: "Student",
    con: "Contractor",
    men: "Mentor",
    dex: "Dean",
    sup: "Super-Admin"
  }.freeze, T::Hash[Symbol, String])

  # Latin-letter role chips for the navbar scope indicator.
  # See #role_glyph for the CC-6 design-review rationale.
  ROLE_GLYPHS = T.let({
    stu: "S",
    con: "C",
    men: "M",
    dex: "D",
    sup: "A"
  }.freeze, T::Hash[Symbol, String])

  # Characters reserved by design-system §5.2 for the activity
  # / submission status channel. The role chip MUST NOT emit
  # any of these characters (CC-6 design-review closure).
  STATUS_RESERVED_GLYPHS = T.let(%w[
    ○ ◐ ◑ ◉ ◷ ◴ ◵ ◶ ✓ ✔ ★ ☆ ↺ ↻ ⊙ ⊚
  ].join.freeze, String)

  # Returns a scope hash keyed by the type of resource the caller
  # needs. :students is the canonical list. :site is the actor's
  # active site (nil if no site is in scope, e.g. a super-admin
  # whose active_site spans the whole org).
  #
  # active_role: / active_site: kwargs override the user-record
  # fallback so controllers can pass the switched (role, site)
  # tuple from the session / CurrentAttributes. Without this
  # override the resolver would always derive scope from the
  # persisted user.role + user.site, which contradicts the
  # RP-W3 role switcher contract. When the kwargs are nil
  # (e.g. a unit test that has no session), the resolver falls
  # back to active_role(user) / active_site(user) so legacy
  # callers and unit tests still work.
  #
  # Every key in the returned hash is filtered to the ACTIVE
  # SITE for site-scoped roles (:con, :men, :dex). Site-wide
  # roles (:stu, :sup) honor the actor's record directly.
  # Previously the :con and :men branches returned scopes that
  # crossed sites (a contractor with Oak + Pine assignments
  # saw both at once; a mentor whose mentored classes included
  # a Pine class leaked Pine students). Now the active site is
  # the bounding box for every site-scoped role.
  sig { params(user: T.nilable(User), active_role: T.nilable(Role), active_site: T.nilable(Site)).returns(Scope) }
  def self.call(user, active_role: nil, active_site: nil)
    return empty_scope(active_site) if user.nil?

    role = (active_role || active_role(user))&.to_sym
    site = active_site || active_site(user)

    case role
    when :stu
      classes = user.classes.where(site_id: site&.id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: [ user.id ], class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: User.where(id: user.id),
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
        site: site
      }
    when :con
      # Contractors are site-scoped. Only ContractorSupport rows
      # at the ACTIVE site count. Without this scope a
      # contractor supporting students at Oak + Pine would see
      # both, which leaks across the RP-W3 site switcher.
      #
      # Defense-in-depth (analysis feedback G-security-1): even
      # though the ContractorSupport model validates site_id
      # consistency, this scope adds an extra filter to assert
      # that the joined student row is actually at the active
      # site. A malformed cross-site row that slipped past the
      # model check (e.g. a raw insert or race) is
      # still invisible. The same filter is applied to classes
      # and submissions so a stale join cannot leak off-site
      # records via either pathway.
      student_ids = user.contractor_supports
                          .where(site_id: site&.id)
                          .pluck(:student_id)
      student_ids = User.where(id: student_ids, site_id: site&.id).pluck(:id)
      classes = SchoolClass.where(id: Enrollment.where(student_id: student_ids).select(:school_class_id),
                                  site_id: site&.id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: User.where(id: student_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
        site: site
      }
    when :men
      # Mentor scope is filtered to the ACTIVE site so a
      # mentor who taught at a different site historically
      # (e.g. moved sites) cannot leak students from the
      # previous site. Student scope is further limited to
      # enrollments active on the school's local date; the
      # date_left boundary is half-open: a student is no longer
      # active on date_left. Legacy rows with no start date remain
      # active until they have a date_left boundary.
      class_ids = user.school_classes_as_mentor
                       .where(site_id: site&.id)
                       .pluck(:id)
      school_date = site&.today || Date.current
      student_ids = Enrollment.active_on(school_date, site: site)
                              .where(school_class_id: class_ids)
                              .distinct
                              .pluck(:student_id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: class_ids)
      {
        students: User.where(id: student_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        classes: SchoolClass.where(id: class_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: user.school_classes_as_mentor.where(site_id: site&.id),
        site: site
      }
    when :dex
      students = User.where(role: :stu, site_id: site&.id)
      student_ids = students.select(:id)
      classes = SchoolClass.where(site_id: site&.id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: students,
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: classes,
        site: site
      }
    when :sup
      # Per-site differentiation for super-admin (AC-01): narrow
      # every student-record scope to the ACTIVE site only. Cross-
      # site admin surfaces (SitesController#sites_in_scope,
      # RolesController#manageable_sites) remain org-wide — those
      # are controller-private methods that query
      # Site.where(organization: org) directly, independent of
      # SiteScopeResolver. The :site return value still carries
      # the active Site so views / presenters that read it for
      # the navbar + scope indicator see the operator's current
      # site, not a synthetic org marker.
      site_ids = site ? [ site.id ] : []
      students = User.where(role: :stu, site_id: site_ids)
      student_ids = students.select(:id)
      classes = SchoolClass.where(site_id: site_ids)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: students,
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: classes,
        site: site
      }
    else
      {
        students: User.none,
        classes: SchoolClass.none,
        submissions: Submission.none,
        daily_reflections: DailyReflection.none,
        school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
        site: site
      }
    end
  end

  sig do
    params(student_ids: IdFilter, class_ids: IdFilter)
      .returns(RecordScopes)
  end
  def self.plan_activity_records(student_ids:, class_ids:)
    # Submissions moved to the evidence tree in ac8bda94: the join is
    # now Submission -> activity (Activity) -> milestone -> round -> plans
    # -> school_class. The previous Submission -> plan_activity
    # (PlanActivity) hop no longer exists (plan_activity_id was dropped
    # from the submissions table), so we use Submission.for_class's
    # canonical chain (the same join shape school_class.rb#submissions
    # uses today). DailyReflection still keeps plan_activity_id so the
    # original plan-tree hop is preserved for that relation.
    submissions = Submission
                  .joins(activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                  .where(student_id: student_ids, plans: { school_class_id: class_ids })
                  .where("plans.student_id = submissions.student_id")
                  .where("plans.round_id = rounds.id")
                  # Resolver-owned evidence milestones are plan-specific. Joining
                  # only through the shared round lets a student's sibling AM/PM
                  # submission match any one of that student's plans in a mentor
                  # class. Bind this activity to its exact plan before applying
                  # the class scope.
                  .where("milestones.title = ('Evidence for plan ' || plans.id::text)")
                  .where("rounds.site_id = school_classes.site_id")
    daily_reflections = DailyReflection
                        .joins(plan_activity: { plan: %i[school_class round] })
                        .where(student_id: student_ids, plans: { school_class_id: class_ids })
                        .where("plans.student_id = daily_reflections.student_id")
                        .where("rounds.site_id = school_classes.site_id")

    { submissions: submissions, daily_reflections: daily_reflections }
  end
  private_class_method :plan_activity_records

  # Active (role, site) tuple for the request. Returns a Hash
  # with :role (Symbol) + :site (Site | nil). Pulls from the
  # optional kwargs first (so callers pass session values), then
  # falls back to the persisted user record. This is the
  # canonical helper for any controller that needs both values
  # at once without two separate calls.
  sig do
    params(user: User, active_role: T.nilable(Symbol), active_site: T.nilable(Site))
      .returns(ActiveScope)
  end
  def self.active_scope_for(user, active_role: nil, active_site: nil)
    {
      role: T.must(active_role || active_role(user)).to_sym,
      site: active_site || active_site(user)
    }
  end

  # Role hierarchy for selecting highest-privilege active role.
  # Higher number = higher privilege (per spec 01 RP-5).
  ROLE_HIERARCHY = T.let({ stu: 0, con: 1, men: 2, dex: 3, sup: 4 }.freeze, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])

  # The actor's effective role. For single-role accounts this is
  # the persisted `role` column. For multi-role accounts it selects
  # the highest-privilege role at the active site per spec 01 RP-5:
  #   "On login, route a user to the home surface of their
  #   highest-privilege active role."
  #
  # Selection order:
  #   1. Prefer a UserRole at the active site whose role matches
  #      the user's persisted role column (so the persisted role
  #      is the canonical anchor for the default landing page).
  #   2. Otherwise, select the highest-privilege UserRole at the
  #      active site using ROLE_HIERARCHY (stu < con < men < dex < sup).
  #   3. Otherwise, the highest-privilege UserRole across all sites.
  #   4. Otherwise, the persisted role column.
  #
  # SECURITY (AC analysis feedback): the persisted `role`
  # fallback in step 4 used to be unconditional. A user whose
  # persisted role column was `:men` could keep mentor access
  # AFTER an admin revoked their `:men` UserRole row — the
  # resolver would re-discover the staff role via the
  # persisted column and the require_staff /
  # require_credit_authority gates would accept the request.
  # The fix downgrades the persisted-column fallback for
  # STAFF roles (:con / :men / :dex / :sup) to :stu so a
  # revocation always takes effect: once a UserRole row is
  # created and later destroyed, the persisted column alone
  # cannot grant staff capability. Students (:stu) still
  # use the persisted column as the fallback (their access
  # boundary is roster enrollment, not role grants, and
  # requiring a UserRole for every student would force a
  # backfill of the entire existing student roster).
  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(Symbol)) }
  def self.active_role(user)
    effective = effective_user_role(user)
    return effective.role.to_sym if effective

    persisted_role = user.role.to_sym
    # SECURITY: a persisted staff role with NO live UserRole
    # grant is treated as :stu. The revocation safety net
    # only applies to staff roles; students keep their
    # persisted role as the fallback because their access
    # boundary is Enrollment (not UserRole) and back-filling
    # UserRole rows for every student would be a separate
    # migration that is out of scope here.
    return :stu unless persisted_role == :stu
    persisted_role
  end

  # The actor's active site. It is derived from the same
  # effective UserRole tuple as active_role, so a user whose
  # persisted primary site is student-only but who holds a staff
  # UserRole at another site signs in as that staff (role, site)
  # pair instead of mixing the staff role with the stale primary
  # site.
  #
  # SECURITY (AC analysis feedback): the persisted `site`
  # fallback used to be unconditional. A user whose persisted
  # site column was Oak Campus could keep Oak access AFTER an
  # admin revoked their Oak UserRole rows (e.g. moved to Pine
  # or off-boarded) — the resolver would re-discover the Oak
  # site via the persisted column. The fix returns nil for the
  # persisted-site fallback when there are NO UserRoles for
  # the user (so legacy single-role users still get their
  # persisted site for backwards compatibility) AND when the
  # user has UserRoles but none of them are at the persisted
  # site (so the persisted site cannot authorize a stale
  # access). For users with a UserRole at the persisted site
  # the fallback still returns the persisted site (the
  # canonical site IS the persisted one). The caller-side
  # gates that need a non-nil site (require_staff,
  # require_admin, require_credit_authority) already fail closed when
  # active_site is nil, so a nil return is the safe default
  # for the cross-tenant gap case.
  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(Site)) }
  def self.active_site(user)
    return nil if user.nil?

    effective = effective_user_role(user)
    return effective.site if effective

    # Fallback: user has no UserRoles (legacy single-role
    # account). Use persisted site for back-compat.
    user.site
  end

  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(UserRole)) }
  def self.effective_user_role(user)
    return nil if user.user_roles.empty?

    roles = user.user_roles.includes(:site).to_a
    staff_role = highest_role(roles.reject { |ur| ur.role.to_sym == :stu }, user)
    return staff_role if staff_role

    highest_role(roles, user)
  end
  private_class_method :effective_user_role

  sig { params(roles: T::Array[UserRole], user: User).returns(T.nilable(UserRole)) }
  def self.highest_role(roles, user)
    roles.max_by do |user_role|
      [
        ROLE_HIERARCHY[user_role.role.to_sym] || -1,
        user_role.site_id == user.site_id ? 1 : 0,
        -user_role.id.to_i
      ]
    end
  end
  private_class_method :highest_role

  sig { params(site: T.nilable(Site)).returns(Scope) }
  def self.empty_scope(site)
    {
      students: User.none,
      classes: SchoolClass.none,
      submissions: Submission.none,
      daily_reflections: DailyReflection.none,
      school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
      site: site
    }
  end
  private_class_method :empty_scope

  # Canonical role label per spec 01 §3, used in the navbar
  # scope indicator and the dev login chip.
  sig { params(role: T.any(Symbol, String)).returns(String) }
  def self.role_label(role)
    ROLE_LABELS[role.to_sym] || role.to_s
  end

  # Glyph rendered in the navbar scope indicator. Spec 01
  # RP-W5 says non-CON gets the role label, CON gets the
  # persistent "monitoring/support only" cue (so a contractor
  # sees that they are NOT in the credit-authority chain).
  #
  # AC (analysis feedback, design-review CC-6 closure): the
  # previous implementation reused status-pill glyphs (◐ / ○
  # / ◑ / ◉ / ★) for the role chip. design-system §5.2 reserves
  # those characters for activity/submission STATUS (NOT
  # STARTED, IN REVIEW, SELECTED, etc.) — the role chip and the
  # status pill must NOT share a glyph channel because a reader
  # scanning for review state would misread the role chip.
  # The fix uses Latin-letter role chips (S/M/C/D/A) which are
  # unambiguous against the status channel.
  sig { params(role: T.any(Symbol, String)).returns(String) }
  def self.role_glyph(role)
    case role.to_sym
    when :con then "C"
    when :stu then "S"
    when :men then "M"
    when :dex then "D"
    when :sup then "A"
    else "•"
    end
  end
end

      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: User.where(id: student_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
        site: site
      }
    when :men
      # Mentor scope is filtered to the ACTIVE site so a
      # mentor who taught at a different site historically
      # (e.g. moved sites) cannot leak students from the
      # previous site. Student scope is further limited to
      # enrollments active on the school's local date; the
      # date_left boundary is half-open: a student is no longer
      # active on date_left. Legacy rows with no start date remain
      # active until they have a date_left boundary.
      class_ids = user.school_classes_as_mentor
                       .where(site_id: site&.id)
                       .pluck(:id)
      school_date = site&.today || Date.current
      student_ids = Enrollment.active_on(school_date, site: site)
                              .where(school_class_id: class_ids)
                              .distinct
                              .pluck(:student_id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: class_ids)
      {
        students: User.where(id: student_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        classes: SchoolClass.where(id: class_ids, site_id: site&.id),
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: user.school_classes_as_mentor.where(site_id: site&.id),
        site: site
      }
    when :dex
      students = User.where(role: :stu, site_id: site&.id)
      student_ids = students.select(:id)
      classes = SchoolClass.where(site_id: site&.id)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: students,
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: classes,
        site: site
      }
    when :sup
      # Per-site differentiation for super-admin (AC-01): narrow
      # every student-record scope to the ACTIVE site only. Cross-
      # site admin surfaces (SitesController#sites_in_scope,
      # RolesController#manageable_sites) remain org-wide — those
      # are controller-private methods that query
      # Site.where(organization: org) directly, independent of
      # SiteScopeResolver. The :site return value still carries
      # the active Site so views / presenters that read it for
      # the navbar + scope indicator see the operator's current
      # site, not a synthetic org marker.
      site_ids = site ? [ site.id ] : []
      students = User.where(role: :stu, site_id: site_ids)
      student_ids = students.select(:id)
      classes = SchoolClass.where(site_id: site_ids)
      records = plan_activity_records(student_ids: student_ids, class_ids: classes.select(:id))
      {
        students: students,
        classes: classes,
        submissions: records.fetch(:submissions),
        daily_reflections: records.fetch(:daily_reflections),
        school_classes_as_mentor: classes,
        site: site
      }
    else
      {
        students: User.none,
        classes: SchoolClass.none,
        submissions: Submission.none,
        daily_reflections: DailyReflection.none,
        school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
        site: site
      }
    end
  end

  sig do
    params(student_ids: IdFilter, class_ids: IdFilter)
      .returns(RecordScopes)
  end
  def self.plan_activity_records(student_ids:, class_ids:)
    # Submissions moved to the evidence tree in ac8bda94: the join is
    # now Submission -> activity (Activity) -> milestone -> round -> plans
    # -> school_class. The previous Submission -> plan_activity
    # (PlanActivity) hop no longer exists (plan_activity_id was dropped
    # from the submissions table), so we use Submission.for_class's
    # canonical chain (the same join shape school_class.rb#submissions
    # uses today). DailyReflection still keeps plan_activity_id so the
    # original plan-tree hop is preserved for that relation.
    submissions = Submission
                  .joins(activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                  .where(student_id: student_ids, plans: { school_class_id: class_ids })
                  .where("plans.student_id = submissions.student_id")
                  .where("plans.round_id = rounds.id")
                  # Resolver-owned evidence milestones are plan-specific. Joining
                  # only through the shared round lets a student's sibling AM/PM
                  # submission match any one of that student's plans in a mentor
                  # class. Bind this activity to its exact plan before applying
                  # the class scope.
                  .where("milestones.title = ('Evidence for plan ' || plans.id::text)")
                  .where("rounds.site_id = school_classes.site_id")
    daily_reflections = DailyReflection
                        .joins(plan_activity: { plan: %i[school_class round] })
                        .where(student_id: student_ids, plans: { school_class_id: class_ids })
                        .where("plans.student_id = daily_reflections.student_id")
                        .where("rounds.site_id = school_classes.site_id")

    { submissions: submissions, daily_reflections: daily_reflections }
  end
  private_class_method :plan_activity_records

  # Active (role, site) tuple for the request. Returns a Hash
  # with :role (Symbol) + :site (Site | nil). Pulls from the
  # optional kwargs first (so callers pass session values), then
  # falls back to the persisted user record. This is the
  # canonical helper for any controller that needs both values
  # at once without two separate calls.
  sig do
    params(user: User, active_role: T.nilable(Symbol), active_site: T.nilable(Site))
      .returns(ActiveScope)
  end
  def self.active_scope_for(user, active_role: nil, active_site: nil)
    {
      role: T.must(active_role || active_role(user)).to_sym,
      site: active_site || active_site(user)
    }
  end

  # Role hierarchy for selecting highest-privilege active role.
  # Higher number = higher privilege (per spec 01 RP-5).
  ROLE_HIERARCHY = T.let({ stu: 0, con: 1, men: 2, dex: 3, sup: 4 }.freeze, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])

  # The actor's effective role. For single-role accounts this is
  # the persisted `role` column. For multi-role accounts it selects
  # the highest-privilege role at the active site per spec 01 RP-5:
  #   "On login, route a user to the home surface of their
  #   highest-privilege active role."
  #
  # Selection order:
  #   1. Prefer a UserRole at the active site whose role matches
  #      the user's persisted role column (so the persisted role
  #      is the canonical anchor for the default landing page).
  #   2. Otherwise, select the highest-privilege UserRole at the
  #      active site using ROLE_HIERARCHY (stu < con < men < dex < sup).
  #   3. Otherwise, the highest-privilege UserRole across all sites.
  #   4. Otherwise, the persisted role column.
  #
  # SECURITY (AC analysis feedback): the persisted `role`
  # fallback in step 4 used to be unconditional. A user whose
  # persisted role column was `:men` could keep mentor access
  # AFTER an admin revoked their `:men` UserRole row — the
  # resolver would re-discover the staff role via the
  # persisted column and the require_staff /
  # require_credit_authority gates would accept the request.
  # The fix downgrades the persisted-column fallback for
  # STAFF roles (:con / :men / :dex / :sup) to :stu so a
  # revocation always takes effect: once a UserRole row is
  # created and later destroyed, the persisted column alone
  # cannot grant staff capability. Students (:stu) still
  # use the persisted column as the fallback (their access
  # boundary is roster enrollment, not role grants, and
  # requiring a UserRole for every student would force a
  # backfill of the entire existing student roster).
  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(Symbol)) }
  def self.active_role(user)
    effective = effective_user_role(user)
    return effective.role.to_sym if effective

    persisted_role = user.role.to_sym
    # SECURITY: a persisted staff role with NO live UserRole
    # grant is treated as :stu. The revocation safety net
    # only applies to staff roles; students keep their
    # persisted role as the fallback because their access
    # boundary is Enrollment (not UserRole) and back-filling
    # UserRole rows for every student would be a separate
    # migration that is out of scope here.
    return :stu unless persisted_role == :stu
    persisted_role
  end

  # The actor's active site. It is derived from the same
  # effective UserRole tuple as active_role, so a user whose
  # persisted primary site is student-only but who holds a staff
  # UserRole at another site signs in as that staff (role, site)
  # pair instead of mixing the staff role with the stale primary
  # site.
  #
  # SECURITY (AC analysis feedback): the persisted `site`
  # fallback used to be unconditional. A user whose persisted
  # site column was Oak Campus could keep Oak access AFTER an
  # admin revoked their Oak UserRole rows (e.g. moved to Pine
  # or off-boarded) — the resolver would re-discover the Oak
  # site via the persisted column. The fix returns nil for the
  # persisted-site fallback when there are NO UserRoles for
  # the user (so legacy single-role users still get their
  # persisted site for backwards compatibility) AND when the
  # user has UserRoles but none of them are at the persisted
  # site (so the persisted site cannot authorize a stale
  # access). For users with a UserRole at the persisted site
  # the fallback still returns the persisted site (the
  # canonical site IS the persisted one). The caller-side
  # gates that need a non-nil site (require_staff,
  # require_admin, require_credit_authority) already fail closed when
  # active_site is nil, so a nil return is the safe default
  # for the cross-tenant gap case.
  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(Site)) }
  def self.active_site(user)
    return nil if user.nil?

    effective = effective_user_role(user)
    return effective.site if effective

    # Fallback: user has no UserRoles (legacy single-role
    # account). Use persisted site for back-compat.
    user.site
  end

  sig { params(user: User).returns(T.nilable(UserRole)) }
  def self.effective_user_role(user)
    return nil if user.user_roles.empty?

    roles = user.user_roles.includes(:site).to_a
    staff_role = highest_role(roles.reject { |ur| ur.role.to_sym == :stu }, user)
    return staff_role if staff_role

    highest_role(roles, user)
  end
  private_class_method :effective_user_role

  sig { params(roles: T::Array[UserRole], user: User).returns(T.nilable(UserRole)) }
  def self.highest_role(roles, user)
    roles.max_by do |user_role|
      [
        ROLE_HIERARCHY[user_role.role.to_sym] || -1,
        user_role.site_id == user.site_id ? 1 : 0,
        -user_role.id.to_i
      ]
    end
  end
  private_class_method :highest_role

  sig { params(site: T.nilable(Site)).returns(Scope) }
  def self.empty_scope(site)
    {
      students: User.none,
      classes: SchoolClass.none,
      submissions: Submission.none,
      daily_reflections: DailyReflection.none,
      school_classes_as_mentor: SchoolClass.none,
      site: site
    }
  end
  private_class_method :empty_scope

  # Canonical role label per spec 01 §3, used in the navbar
  # scope indicator and the dev login chip.
  sig { params(role: T.any(Symbol, String)).returns(String) }
  def self.role_label(role)
    ROLE_LABELS[role.to_sym] || role.to_s
  end

  # Glyph rendered in the navbar scope indicator. Spec 01
  # RP-W5 says non-CON gets the role label, CON gets the
  # persistent "monitoring/support only" cue (so a contractor
  # sees that they are NOT in the credit-authority chain).
  #
  # AC (analysis feedback, design-review CC-6 closure): the
  # previous implementation reused status-pill glyphs (◐ / ○
  # / ◑ / ◉ / ★) for the role chip. design-system §5.2 reserves
  # those characters for activity/submission STATUS (NOT
  # STARTED, IN REVIEW, SELECTED, etc.) — the role chip and the
  # status pill must NOT share a glyph channel because a reader
  # scanning for review state would misread the role chip.
  # The fix uses Latin-letter role chips (S/M/C/D/A) which are
  # unambiguous against the status channel.
  sig { params(role: T.any(Symbol, String)).returns(String) }
  def self.role_glyph(role)
    case role.to_sym
    when :con then "C"
    when :stu then "S"
    when :men then "M"
    when :dex then "D"
    when :sup then "A"
    else "•"
    end
  end
end

class Submission < ApplicationRecord

  enum :content_scope, { supporting: 0, work_product: 1 }, prefix: true

  belongs_to :student, class_name: "User"
  # WT-03 / S-9 — evidence destination. The +activity+ association
  # is optional so a student can capture work without first picking
  # a destination (§6 PRODUCT_CRITERIA). When the row is filed, the
  # activity is set via Students::Filing#file!. The sole permanent
  # cross-tree FK is activity_log_entries.plan_activity_id.
  belongs_to :activity, optional: true
  # WT-11 / S-13 / NEXT-2 — back-compat writer. Rails still receives
  # legacy plan-tree assignments from established callers, so resolve them at
  # the model boundary and persist only the canonical evidence-tree Activity.
  sig { params(value: T.nilable(T.any(Activity, PlanActivity))).void }
  def activity=(value)
    self.legacy_plan_activity_assignment = value if value.is_a?(PlanActivity)
    super(value.is_a?(PlanActivity) ? Students::EvidenceActivityResolver.for_plan_activity!(value) : value)
  end

  # WT-11 / S-13 / NEXT-2 — back-compat reader. The legacy
  # +Submission#plan_activity+ was retired when the FK column was
  # renamed to +activity_id+, but tests, system specs, and the
  # broader Rails surface still read +submission.plan_activity+ as
  # the matching plan-tree PlanActivity. Bridge through the
  # evidence-tree +activity+ back to the matching PlanActivity by
  # round + scheduled_on + title so legacy assertions keep
  # returning a PlanActivity without restoring the removed FK
  # column.
  sig { returns(T.nilable(PlanActivity)) }
  def plan_activity
    resolved = activity&.plan_activity || legacy_plan_activity_assignment
    return resolved if resolved

    evidence_activity = activity
    student_record = student
    return nil unless evidence_activity && student_record

    Students::EvidenceActivityResolver.legacy_plan_activity_for(evidence_activity, student: student_record)
  end

  # Read-only compatibility projection for legacy callers that identify a
  # submission by its plan-tree activity. The persisted foreign key remains
  # activity_id; exposing this derived id does not restore the removed column.
  sig { returns(T.nilable(Integer)) }
  def plan_activity_id
    plan_activity&.id

  def require_student
    return if current_student
    redirect_to login_redirect_path, alert: "Please sign in as a student."
  end

  sig { void }
  def require_staff
    if current_staff
      # The session-stored active role may already be a staff
      # role (the UserRole chain is intact) BUT the actor's
      # PERSISTED role column may be :stu — a recovery actor
      # whose persisted role was downgraded by the spec 01
      # revocation safety net. We still accept the request
      # because the live UserRole grant authorizes the action;
      # no scope-side redirect fires.
      return true

# typed: strict

# Contractor /support surface (EV-W7, EV-W8, EV-25..EV-31).
#
# The contractor's daily monitoring tracker + per-student support view.
# Authoritative absence: NO approve / return / retract / credit
# actions are defined here. The
# require_credit_authority gate on ReviewsController already blocks
# :con, and SupportController intentionally does not define any
# of the credit write actions so a contractor cannot
# even reach a controller method that would change a submission
# status.
#
# Persistence model: contractor support notes are CANONICAL Comments
# (visibility: :staff_internal, commentable: the student User) per
# spec 09 CN-16. The Comment model owns the staff_internal scope +
# the support_notes_for(student) convenience scope (see
# app/models/comment.rb). There is intentionally NO SupportRecord
# model, NO support_records table, and NO note:text column — this
# is the single canonical note system.
#
# The presence indicator (EV-W8 "On campus?") is encoded in the
# comment body by #format_support_body, not stored as a separate
# column. Decoding lives in SupportNotesHelper (display-only).
class SupportController < ApplicationController
  extend T::Sig

  NOT_STARTED_STATUS = T.let("not_started".freeze, String)

  sig { void }
  def initialize
    super
    @scope = T.let(nil, T.nilable(SiteScopeResolver::Scope))
    @today_states = T.let({}, T::Hash[User, Symbol])
    @needs_nudge_by_student = T.let({}, T::Hash[User, T::Boolean])
    @attendance_by_student = T.let({}, T::Hash[User, T.nilable(ContractorAttendance)])
    @open_items_by_student = T.let({}, T::Hash[User, Integer])
    @filter = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Symbol))
    @q = T.let("", String)
    @all_assigned_students_count = T.let(0, Integer)
    @expected_students_count = T.let(0, Integer)
    @daily_counts = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
    @export_counts = T.let({}, T::Hash[Symbol, Integer])
    @daily_snapshot = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Support::DailySnapshot::Result))
    @assigned_students = T.let([], T::Array[User])
    @current_enrollment_by_student_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[Integer, Enrollment])
    @show_current_enrollment = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Enrollment))
    @show_course_name = T.let(nil, T.nilable(String))
    @show_round_name = T.let(nil, T.nilable(String))
    @show_day_part = T.let(nil, T.nilable(String))
    @student = T.let(nil, T.nilable(User))
    @support_notes = T.let(Comment.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
    @support_notes_by_date = T.let({}, T::Hash[Date, T::Array[Comment]])
    @recent_submissions = T.let([], T::Array[Submission])
    @latest_submission = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Submission))
    @status_counts = T.let({}, T::Hash[Integer, Integer])
    @daily_reflections = T.let(DailyReflection.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
    @recent_evidence = T.let(EvidenceArtifact.none, ActiveRecord::Relation)
    @recent_evidence_plan_activities_by_id = T.let({}, T::Hash[Integer, T.nilable(PlanActivity)])
    @pending_evidence_count = T.let(0, Integer)
    @activity_statuses = T.let([], T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, Object]])
    @gaps = T.let([], T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, Object]])
    @session_day = T.let(nil, T.nilable(Planning::SessionDay::Result))
  end

  # EV-W7 / EV-W8 / AC-01 — the contractor /support surface is
  # contractor-only. We use `require_contractor` (not
  # `require_staff`) so mentors / deans / super-admins are
  # bounced off /support rather than landing on a
  # contractor-flavored dashboard. `require_authentication`
  # (declared as a top-level before_action in
  # ApplicationController) still fires first so a student
  # visitor is redirected to the student login before the
  # contractor check runs — a contractor-less actor therefore
  # cannot reach any contractor-scoped data through this
  # controller.
  before_action :require_contractor

  # EV-W7 / EV-31 — daily monitoring tracker.
  # Reads the contractor's assigned student list DIRECTLY from
  # SiteScopeResolver#call (the canonical ContractorSupport-derived
  # set at the active site). Does NOT expand via Enrollment — the
  # prior version did, which silently pulled in classmates of
  # assigned students and was the cross-tenant leak fixed in
  # Staff::StudentsController#index.
  #
  # Filter contract (AC-01): the optional `params[:filter]` query
  # string scopes the visible student list to one of the four
  # canonical today-state buckets:
  #
  #   submitted   — :submitted_today
  #   nothing     — :nothing_today
  #   needs_revision — :needs_revision_outstanding
  #   off_campus  — :off_campus_today
  #   (omitted / empty / "all") — no filter, show all assigned students
  #
  # The today-state map is computed for the FULL assigned set so
  # the today-summary cards (Need a nudge / Submitted today /
  # Off campus today) continue to reflect the whole population,
  # not the filtered view — the cards are an aggregate of the
  # whole daily monitoring picture, independent of the user's
  # current filter selection.
  sig { void }
  def index
    actor = T.must(current_user)
    scope_hash = SiteScopeResolver.call(
      actor,
      active_role: current_active_role,
      active_site: current_active_site
    )
    @scope = scope_hash
    all_students = scope_hash[:students].includes(:schedule_blocks, :site).order(:name).to_a
    submission_scope = scope_hash[:submissions]
    submissions_by_student_id = submission_scope
                                 .where(student_id: all_students.map(&:id))
                                 .to_a
                                 .group_by(&:student_id)

    # Today-state per assigned student (EV-31): submitted_today /
    # nothing_today / needs_revision_outstanding / off_campus_today.
    # The current_date is the canonical today (deterministic via
    # Time.current). A contractor sees the local-tz state for
    # their students; the student :participation_model + a matching
    # :schedule_block for today's day_part determines
    # on_campus / off_campus. The map is computed for the FULL
    # set so the summary cards stay correct regardless of filter.
    site = T.must(current_active_site)
    today = site.today
    @session_day = Planning::SessionDay.for(site:, date: today)
    daily_snapshot = Support::DailySnapshot.new(actor:, site:, active_role: T.must(current_active_role)).call
    @daily_snapshot = daily_snapshot
    snapshot_rows_by_student_id = daily_snapshot.rows.index_by { |row| row.student.id }
    @expected_students_count = daily_snapshot.rows.count(&:expected)
    # DA-004 — every X-of-Y numerator must use the SAME
    # denominator the metric is rendered against. Prior versions
    # counted `submitted_today` and `nudged` across ALL assigned
    # rows (including off-campus / no-session students) but
    # rendered the fraction against `@expected_students_count`.
    # An off-campus student that nevertheless submitted evidence
    # would silently inflate the count above its denominator
    # (e.g. 2 of 1). We count each metric over the explicit
    # expected-student subset so every fraction is truthful.
    expected_rows = daily_snapshot.rows.select(&:expected)
    @daily_counts = {
      attendance_recorded: expected_rows.count(&:attendance_recorded?),
      present: expected_rows.count { |row| row.attendance&.state == "present" },
      submitted_today: expected_rows.count(&:submitted_today),
      need_evidence: expected_rows.count(&:needs_evidence?),
      need_nudge: expected_rows.count(&:needs_nudge?),
      nudged: expected_rows.count(&:nudged)
    }
    @today_states = all_students.index_with do |student|
      snapshot_rows_by_student_id.fetch(student.id).state
    end
    @attendance_by_student = all_students.index_with do |student|
      snapshot_rows_by_student_id.fetch(student.id).attendance
    end

    # Contractor "needs a nudge" marker (EV-W7): the canonical snapshot
    # requires no qualifying evidence for an expected student and no
    # staff-internal nudge recorded for that student in the site-local day.
    # Computed over the full assigned set.
    @needs_nudge_by_student = all_students.index_with do |student|
      snapshot_rows_by_student_id.fetch(student.id).needs_nudge?
    end

    # Open-items count per student: current needs-revision outcomes,
    # one per activity. Historical attempts must not keep a resolved
    # revision visible after a newer approved or resubmitted outcome.
    needs_revision_counts = submissions_by_student_id.transform_values do |submissions|
      submissions.group_by(&:activity_id).values.count do |attempts|
        attempts.max_by { |submission| [ submission.attempt_no, submission.created_at, submission.id ] }.status_needs_revision?
      end
    end
    @open_items_by_student = all_students.index_with { |student| needs_revision_counts[student.id].to_i }

    # AC-01 — state filter. Translate the params[:filter] string
    # into a today-state symbol so the view + table renders only
    # students in that bucket. Unknown / blank filter values are
    # treated as "all" (no filter). The mapping is owned by
    # Support::FilterPolicy so a click on a "Submitted today" pill
    # actually narrows the list and the metric pill / export pill
    # set never drifts.
    @filter = Support::FilterPolicy.from_slug(params[:filter])

    # WT-15 / AC-07 — name search via q= ILIKE. Applied AFTER
    # the assigned-student set is resolved but BEFORE the today-
    # state / open-items / needs-nudge maps so the maps always
    # reflect the full assigned population (the today-summary
    # cards are an aggregate, not a filter view). The
    # sanitizer mirrors Staff::StudentsController#index so a
    # future contract update only lands in one place.
    @q = params[:q].to_s
    name_filtered_students = if @q.present?
      all_students.select { |student| student.name.to_s.downcase.include?(@q.downcase) }
    else
      all_students
    end

    @all_assigned_students_count = name_filtered_students.size
    searched_rows = name_filtered_students.map { |student| snapshot_rows_by_student_id.fetch(student.id) }
    @export_counts = Support::FilterPolicy::SUPPORTED_GAP_FILTER_SYMBOLS.index_with do |gap_filter|
      searched_rows.count { |row| Support::FilterPolicy.matches?(row, gap_filter) }
    end
    @assigned_students = if @filter
      name_filtered_students.select do |student|
        row = snapshot_rows_by_student_id.fetch(student.id)
        Support::FilterPolicy.matches?(row, @filter)
      end
    else
      name_filtered_students
    end

    # WT-15 / AC-07 — per-student current-enrollment lookup for
    # the day-part chip column. Pre-built in the controller so
    # the view can render one DayPartTagComponent per row
    # without an N+1 query.
    site = T.must(current_active_site)
    @current_enrollment_by_student_id = Enrollment
                                           .active_on(site.today, site:)
                                           .where(student_id: @assigned_students.map(&:id))
                                           .index_by(&:student_id)
  end

  # Export rows are selected from the same contractor snapshot and active
  # filter contract as the roster. The route has no site or student scope
  # parameters, so forged query strings cannot broaden the report.
  sig { void }
  def export_missing_students
    actor = T.must(current_user)
    site = T.must(current_active_site)
    snapshot = Support::DailySnapshot.new(actor:, site:, active_role: T.must(current_active_role)).call
    filter = Support::FilterPolicy.export_gap(params[:filter])
    rows = snapshot.rows.select { |row| Support::FilterPolicy.matches?(row, filter) }
    query = params[:q].to_s.downcase
    rows = rows.select { |row| row.student.name.to_s.downcase.include?(query) } if query.present?

    SupportExportAudit.create!(actor:, site:, filter: filter.to_s, query: query.truncate(255, omission: ""), row_count: rows.size)

    send_data Support::MissingStudentsExport.call(rows:, site:, filter:),
              type: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
              disposition: "attachment",
              filename: "missing-students-#{T.must(site.slug).parameterize}-#{site.today.iso8601}-#{filter}.xlsx"
  end

  # EV-W8 / EV-30 — per-student support view.
  # Loads the student via the SiteScopeResolver scope so a contractor
  # CANNOT view a non-assigned student (foreign-student access
  # returns 404 via scoped_student_for_show).
  sig { void }
  def show
    student = scoped_student_for_show
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless student
    @student = student

    # S-7 GAP #4 — compact identity strip on the show hero. The
    # contractor must see the canonical course / round / day-part
    # context for the student at a glance, sourced from the same
    # resolver-scoped enrollment data the index roster uses. The
    # first canonical enrollment (newest round start) wins so the
    # strip stays a single line and never duplicates the index's
    # assignment list. A student with no current enrollment renders
    # nothing extra (the hero stays compact), matching the
    # show hero's "display name only" default.
    # Enrollment does not carry the round directly; the canonical
    # round for the active term is the round behind the school's
    # plan rows. We load the plan (includes :round) for the
    # school_class so the lede exposes the same round name the
    # index roster uses.
    # The identity strip must use the same active-site enrollment boundary
    # as the roster. `Enrollment.current` alone can select a newer enrollment
    # from another site for a student with historical/multi-site records,
    # exposing foreign course context on this contractor-scoped surface.
    @show_current_enrollment = Enrollment
                                .active_on(T.must(current_active_site).today, site: T.must(current_active_site))
                                .where(student_id: student.id)
                                .includes(school_class: :course)
                                .order(created_at: :desc)
                                .first
    if @show_current_enrollment
      school_class = @show_current_enrollment.school_class
      @show_course_name = school_class&.course&.name
      @show_day_part = school_class&.day_part_tag.to_s.upcase.presence
      plan = Plan.where(student_id: student.id, school_class_id: @show_current_enrollment.school_class_id)
                 .includes(:round)
                 .order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc)
                 .first
      @show_round_name = plan&.round&.display_label
    end

    @support_notes = student.comments.support_notes_for(student).limit(20)
    # AC-02 — group the support-history rows by calendar date so
    # the per-student view surfaces day-labeled sections instead
    # of a single flat list. Each group is a [date, [comments]]
    # tuple ordered newest-date first; within a date, comments
    # stay newest-first via support_notes_for's DESC order.
    # The grouping lives here (not in the view) so the view
    # stays a pure renderer and a future JSON endpoint can
    # reuse the same shape.
    @support_notes_by_date = @support_notes.group_by { |n| n.created_at.to_date }
    # Recent submissions READ-ONLY — the contractor sees the
    # multi-artifact gallery + reflection via the canonical
    # evidence_artifacts/_gallery partial (rendered with
    # readonly: true so edit/remove/reorder are hidden).
    resolver_scope = SiteScopeResolver.call(
      T.must(current_user),
      active_role: current_active_role,
      active_site: current_active_site
    )
    class_ids = resolver_scope[:classes].pluck(:id)
    submission_scope = resolver_scope[:submissions].where(student_id: student.id)
    latest_outcomes = submission_scope
                      .latest_activity_outcomes
                      .includes(activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                      .to_a
                      .sort_by { |submission| [ submission.submitted_at || submission.created_at, submission.id ] }
                      .reverse
    @recent_submissions = latest_outcomes.first(10)
    @latest_submission = @recent_submissions.first
    @status_counts = latest_outcomes.group_by(&:status_before_type_cast).transform_values(&:size)
    @daily_reflections = resolver_scope[:daily_reflections]
                         .where(student_id: student.id)
                         .includes(plan_activity: { plan: %i[round school_class] })
                         .ordered
    @recent_evidence = EvidenceArtifact.kept
                                       .where(screening_status: :clean, submission_id: submission_scope.select(:id))
                                       .includes(:submission, activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } })
                                       .includes(:submission, activity: { milestone: :round })
                                       .order(captured_at: :desc, id: :desc)
                                       .limit(10)
    @recent_evidence_plan_activities_by_id = build_evidence_artifact_plan_activity_lookup(@recent_evidence.to_a)
    @pending_evidence_count = EvidenceArtifact.kept
                                              .where(screening_status: :pending,
                                                     submission_id: submission_scope.select(:id))
                                              .count

    # GAP-CON-01 / AC-01 — per-activity status table (EV-27
    # 'current per-activity statuses'). The contractor
    # needs to see "Activity A: needs revision, Activity B:
    # not started, Activity C: approved" in one scan so the
    # /support/students/:id surface stays a contractor
    # monitoring primitive (NOT a credit-authority surface —
    # read-only rendering only). The resolver supplies the latest
    # course-scoped submission outcomes, while this query loads the
    # student's planned activities with their course and round.
    # Row objects expose: activity_id (Integer), title (String), round_name
    # (String), status (String — a submission status or not_started).
    enrolled_activities = PlanActivity
                          .joins(plan: %i[round school_class])
                          .where(plans: { student_id: student.id, school_class_id: class_ids })
                          .includes(plan: %i[round school_class])
                          .order(:position, :id)
    latest_by_plan_activity_id = build_latest_outcomes_index(latest_outcomes)
    @activity_statuses = enrolled_activities.map do |activity|
      latest = latest_by_plan_activity_id[activity.id]
      {
        activity_id: activity.id,
        title: activity.title,
        course_name: activity.plan&.school_class&.name.to_s,
        day_part: activity.plan&.school_class&.day_part_tag.to_s.upcase,
        round_name: activity.plan&.round&.display_label.to_s,
        status: latest&.status.to_s.presence || NOT_STARTED_STATUS
      }
    end
    @gaps = @activity_statuses.select { |row| row[:status] == NOT_STARTED_STATUS }
  end

  sig { params(latest_outcomes: T::Array[Submission]).returns(T::Hash[Integer, Submission]) }
  def build_latest_outcomes_index(latest_outcomes)
    activity_ids = latest_outcomes.filter_map(&:activity_id).uniq
    return {} if activity_ids.empty?
    student = T.must(@student)
    latest_outcomes.each_with_object({}) do |submission, memo|
      plan_activity = submission.activity&.plan_activity
      next unless plan_activity&.plan&.student_id == student.id

      # `latest_outcomes` is ordered newest-first. Preserve that first
      # canonical outcome instead of allowing a historical submission for the
      # same planned activity to overwrite the current contractor-facing state.
      memo[T.must(plan_activity).id] ||= submission
    end
  end

  # EV-W8 / CN-16 — persist a contractor support note.
  # The form posts { presence: "Present"|"Not seen", note: "..." }.
  # We build a Comment with visibility: :staff_internal attached
  # to the student User. The body is formatted to encode the
  # presence label + the free-text note so a future reader of
  # the handoff summary / review context sees both. The Comment
  # model enforces body presence + length (max 5000).
  sig { void }
  def create_note
    student = scoped_student_for_show
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless student
    @student = student

    Support::NoteWriter.call(
      actor: T.must(current_user),
      student: student,
      site: T.must(current_active_site),
      presence: params[:presence].to_s,
      note: params[:note].to_s
    )
    redirect_to support_student_path(student), notice: "Support record saved."
  rescue ArgumentError
    redirect_to support_student_path(student), alert: "Choose a valid support status."
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    redirect_to support_student_path(student),
                alert: error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence.presence ||
                       "Couldn't save that support record."
  end

  # EV-W8 — persist a contractor-only attendance fact for the current
  # active-site day and schedule context. The student lookup is assignment
  # scoped before the writer runs, so forged IDs do not disclose or mutate
  # records outside the contractor's roster.
  sig { void }
  def record_attendance
    student = scoped_student_for_show
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless student

    context = ScheduleContext.for(student)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless context&.on_campus_today

    Support::AttendanceWriter.call(
      actor: T.must(current_user),
      student: student,
      site: T.must(current_active_site),
      local_date: T.must(current_active_site).today,
      day_part: context.current_day_part,
      state: attendance_state_param
    )
    redirect_to support_path, notice: "Attendance saved."
  rescue ArgumentError
    redirect_to support_path, alert: "Choose a valid attendance state."
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    redirect_to support_path, alert: "Couldn't save attendance. Try again."
  end

  # EV-W7 — record an internal nudge event without claiming external delivery.
  sig { void }
  def nudge
    student = scoped_student_for_show
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless student

    Support::NudgeWriter.call(
      actor: T.must(current_user),
      student: student,
      site: T.must(current_active_site)
    )
    redirect_to support_path, notice: "Nudge recorded."
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    redirect_to support_path, alert: "This student is not eligible for a nudge right now."
  end

  private

  sig { returns(Symbol) }
  def attendance_state_param
    state = params[:state].to_s
    raise ArgumentError unless Support::AttendanceWriter::STATES.include?(state)

    state.to_sym
  end

  # Filter slugs, row matching, and export gap handling live in
  # Support::FilterPolicy so the index view, the metric pill
  # links, and the export endpoint all share one source of truth.

  # Authoritatively load a student via the SiteScopeResolver scope
  # so a contractor CANNOT view a non-assigned student. Returns
  # nil on a foreign-student id (the caller renders 404).
  sig { returns(T.nilable(User)) }
  def scoped_student_for_show
    scope_hash = SiteScopeResolver.call(
      T.must(current_user),
      active_role: current_active_role,
      active_site: current_active_site
    )
    scope_hash[:students].find_by(id: params[:id])
  end

  sig { params(artifacts: T::Array[EvidenceArtifact]).returns(T::Hash[Integer, T.nilable(PlanActivity)]) }
  def build_evidence_artifact_plan_activity_lookup(artifacts)
    return {} if artifacts.empty? || @student.nil?
    activity_ids = artifacts.filter_map(&:activity_id).uniq
    return {} if activity_ids.empty?
    activities = Activity.where(id: activity_ids).index_by(&:id)
    artifacts.each_with_object({}) do |artifact, memo|
      activity_id = artifact.activity_id
      activity = artifact.activity || (activity_id && activities[activity_id])
      plan_activity = activity&.plan_activity
      memo[artifact.id] = plan_activity if plan_activity&.plan&.student_id == @student.id
    end
  end
end
